title: Embedding dimensionality orchestration and client compatibility service
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: introduce a safe, observable, and reversible pathway to change embedding vector dimensionality for production indexes and clients while preserving reranking quality and minimizing added latency. This ticket implements an orchestration service and runtime compatibility layer that lets us: (1) serve old and new-dimension requests simultaneously, (2) support in-place/online reindexing with progressive rollouts, and (3) provide client SDK shims and server-side projection fallbacks for backward compatibility. The service will target both our embeddings API and reranking endpoint where dimensional changes impact nearest-neighbor accuracy and rerank rescoring pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility service can accept embeddings queries with legacy dim and produce compatible scores against new-dim indexes within defined quality delta
Canary deployment runs against 1% traffic with automated quality checks (recall@10 / MRR) and latency SLOs enforced
Automated rollback triggers if recall@10 drops > 3% absolute or p99 latency increase > 30ms
Reindex jobs can run online with <5% CPU overhead on serving nodes and throughput >= 500 docs/sec per worker in our standard cluster
Documentation and client SDK adapters published with migration examples and a 3-month deprecation schedule
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Bench & Model: offline projection mapping experiments and dimensionality ablation across 3 representative corpora (kb, dialogs, embeddings-testset)
Phase 1 - Canary: deploy compatibility layer in front of reranker; route 1% queries; run validation harness comparing old-vs-new reranking for same queries
Phase 2 - Warm Reindex: run per-shard incremental reindex at low concurrency; enable query-time projection fallback for shards not yet migrated
Phase 3 - Scale Reindex: increase reindex workers and shift routing; start migrating high-traffic namespaces after gating metrics
Phase 4 - Finalize: complete full reindex, remove projection fallback, bump client SDK default dimension and publish deprecation notice
migration_steps: 1) Offline analysis: compute cosine/inner-product drift between old and candidate new dims using heldout evaluation prompts
2) Train lightweight linear projection (or PCA) + evaluate retrieval/RR metrics to decide pad/truncate vs project approach
3) Implement server-side projection microservice for query-time compatibility (stateless, GPU optional)
4) Add a routing flag in the embeddings service to consult shard-metadata for index-dim and route through projection when needed
5) Launch background reindexer with checkpointing and per-shard QPS-aware throttling
6) Run canary traffic and automated parity checks, iterate on projection model or reindex batch-size
7) Complete migration and remove compatibility paths after 3 successful release cycles
client_impact_and_mitigation: Impact: clients using pinned embedding dimensions in storage or existing vector indices will see inconsistent similarity values until they reindex or use compatibility path
Mitigation: publish SDK adapter that transparently pads/truncates or applies client-side lightweight projection with a feature-flag toggle
Mitigation: provide a CLI reindex tool and managed reindex job for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers
Communication: staged deprecation calendar, per-customer migration support channel, and migration runbooks in Confluence
monitoring_and_slo: Latency SLO: embeddings API p50 < 15ms, p95 < 45ms, p99 < 120ms with projection enabled on path
Rerank quality: recall@10 and MRR delta between baseline and new must be within +/- 3% for gating
Reindex health: per-shard reindex success rate >= 99% and average reindex throughput >= goal
Operational metrics: projection service CPU/GPU utilization, queue latency, error rate, and memory for vector buffers
Alerting: auto rollback if quality delta exceeds threshold or if projection error rate > 0.5%
benchmarks_and_test_plan: Unit tests for projection math (pad/truncate/project) and deterministic output across dims
Integration test: end-to-end rerank pipeline using synthetic queries and real eval sets comparing recall@k
Load test: run reindexer at target concurrency inside staging cluster to measure disk IO and network costs
Latency A/B test during canary with blue/green comparison and traffic shadowing
Back-compat test: run client SDK adapter in CI against older index snapshots to ensure no silent failures
open_risks: Projection-induced semantic drift could reduce rerank relevance for edge queries even if average metrics look OK
Query-time projection increases tail latency and could push reranking past SLOs under burst traffic
Reindex throughput could be limited by disk/network leading to prolonged migration windows and higher cost
Enterprise/private deployments with air-gapped constraints may need bespoke reindex tooling and longer timelines
